newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy hard-left says pensions low reform priority.
newsitem.headline: Italy hard-left says pensions low reform priority.

text.p: Italy's welfare state needs reforms that could lead to increased spending in some areas but pensions should be the last subject discussed in talks, hard left leader Fausto Bertinotti said on Monday.
"We have to carry out real reforms that in some areas, health or education, could also bring increased spending," the Communist Refoundation leader said in a radio interview.

Bertinotti, whose party holds the balance of power in Italy's lower house of parliament and remains outside the centre-left government, said he agreed with the Cgil trade union when "it says that we must talk about pensions last of all."
He said talks on reforms must also take into account "an essential fact: the huge amount of evasion of tax and contributions."
Bertinotti said tackling tax evasion was a priority and suggested certain measures, including taxation on capital flows and strengthening the investigating bodies.
The government has placed welfare reform high on the agenda as it fights to straighten out public finances and win a place in a planned European currency union.
Analysts say it has little option but to cut welfare spending if it is to bring about a lasting reduction in a bloated public sector deficit. -- Rome newsroom 39 6 678 2501
